HR Policy & Procedure Reference

The following pages provide a general reference to Larkspur Films' human resources policies, employee benefits, and standard operating procedures as they relate to production crews. This material supplements the individual personnel records maintained in each employee's file. Where a specific policy is referenced in an offer letter or performance review, the full text of that policy appears below or is available from the HR office upon request.

This addendum is current as of March 14, 2015, and is updated whenever a policy changes. Superseded versions remain on file for audit purposes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1: EMPLOYMENT CLASSIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Larkspur Films classifies all crew members as either:

- Regular Full-Time: Scheduled for 30 or more hours per week, eligible for all benefits.
- Regular Part-Time: Scheduled for fewer than 30 hours per week, eligible for paid sick leave and retirement plan participation after one year of service.
- Project/Temporary: Hired for a specific production or defined period. Not eligible for health benefits; eligible for paid sick leave as required by Oregon law.
- Daily Hire: Engaged for a single day or a short block of days. Not benefits-eligible.

Classification is determined at time of hire and may be reviewed at the start of each new production. If you believe your classification is incorrect, contact HR within 30 days of receiving your first paycheck.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT ELIGIBILITY & I-9 REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

All employees must complete Form I-9 and present acceptable documentation no later than the third business day after their start date. Start date is recorded as the first day on payroll.

If an employee's work authorization expires during employment, HR must be notified at least two weeks prior to the expiration date. The employee is responsible for providing updated documentation. Failure to do so will result in suspension without pay until valid documentation is presented. If documentation cannot be provided within 30 days of suspension, employment will be terminated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3: COMPENSATION & PAYROLL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pay Periods
- Crew members are paid bi-weekly. Payday falls on the Friday following the end of the pay period.
- Timecards are due to the production office by end of day on the Monday following the close of the pay period. Late timecards will be processed on the next pay cycle.

Overtime
- Oregon law requires overtime pay at 1.5 times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek.
- For productions covered by union collective bargaining agreements, overtime rules from the applicable guild contract supersede state law. Consult your department head or HR for specifics.

Per Diem & Reimbursements
- Per diem is paid for out-of-town shoots at a rate of $50 per day. No receipt is required.
- Mileage reimbursement is $0.55 per mile for use of a personal vehicle on company business. A mileage log must be submitted with the expense report.
- All other reimbursable expenses require an itemized receipt. Receipts must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. Expenses submitted after 30 days may be denied.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4: LEAVE POLICIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Paid Sick Leave
Oregon's Sick Time law requires that all employees accrue one hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year. Accrual begins on the first day of employment. Unused sick leave does not carry over to the next calendar year.

**9. ANNUAL MEETING MINUTES**

**9.1 Annual Meeting of Members — March 14, 2025**

The annual meeting of the members of Larkspur Films was held on Friday, March 14, 2025, at 10:00 AM at the company's registered office, 4120 SE Hawthorne Boulevard, Portland, Oregon. The meeting was called to order by Eleanor R. Vasquez, President. Also present were Daniel Okafor, Secretary; Sofia Delgado, Treasurer; and members Hannah Brooks, Aisha Khan, Maya Chen, James Whitfield, Thomas Novak, and Marcus Lee. A quorum was confirmed.

The following matters were presented and acted upon:

- **Approval of Prior Minutes.** The minutes of the annual meeting held March 15, 2024, were read and approved without amendment.
- **President's Report.** Eleanor reviewed the company's activities over the past year, including the completion of principal photography on *Riverbend*, the release of the short film *Harbor Light* to two festival circuits, and the development of two new feature projects. She noted that the company had expanded its post-production capacity in-house, reducing reliance on outside vendors.
- **Treasurer's Report.** Sofia presented the financial statements for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2024. She reported that revenues exceeded expenses, and that the company's cash reserves remained above the board's target threshold. A full copy of the financial statements is available in the office file.
- **Election of Officers.** The members unanimously re-elected Eleanor R. Vasquez as President, Daniel Okafor as Secretary, and Sofia Delgado as Treasurer for the coming year. Hannah Brooks was appointed as Office Manager for another term.
- **New Business.** Discussion was held regarding the company's long-range plan, including exploring co-production opportunities and expanding the development slate. No formal action was taken.

The meeting adjourned at 11:20 AM.

Respectfully submitted,

Daniel Okafor, Secretary

**9.2 Annual Meeting of the Board of Directors — March 14, 2025**

Immediately following the members' meeting, the Board of Directors convened at 11:30 AM. Directors present: Eleanor R. Vasquez, Daniel Okafor, Sofia Delgado, and Hannah Brooks. The board discussed the following items:

- Reviewed the 2025 production schedule and staffing plan.
- Approved a motion to allocate funds for the purchase of a new camera package, subject to final cost estimates.
- Discussed insurance coverage for upcoming shoots; the current policy is adequate for the next two quarters.
- Authorized the President to sign the lease renewal for the office space for an additional three-year term.

The meeting adjourned at 12:15 PM.

**10. COMPANY POLICIES AND PROCEDURES**

**10.1 Expense Reimbursement Policy (Revised March 3, 2025)**

This policy replaces all prior versions. All employees and contractors must submit expense reports within 14 days of incurring the expense. Receipts are required for all expenditures over $25.00. Mileage is reimbursed at the federal rate. Out-of-pocket expenses under $50.00 may be reimbursed from the petty cash fund with a signed receipt. All reimbursement requests must be submitted to Sofia Delgado for approval. Expenses without proper documentation will not be reimbursed.

**10.2 Remote Work Policy (Effective January 6, 2025)**

Employees may work remotely up to two days per week with prior approval from their supervisor. Remote days must be recorded on the shared calendar. All remote work must be performed within the state of Oregon unless otherwise approved. Employees working remotely are expected to be available during core hours of 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM Pacific Time.

Employees are encouraged to share company news on their personal social media accounts, but must not disclose confidential project details, unreleased footage, or financial information. Larkspur Films
Personnel Files — Addendum
HR Policy & Procedure Reference

The following pages provide a general reference to Larkspur Films' human resources policies, employee benefits, and standard operating procedures as they relate to production crews. This material supplements the individual personnel records maintained in each employee's file. Where a specific policy is referenced in an offer letter or performance review, the full text of that policy appears below or is available from the HR office upon request.

This addendum is current as of March 14, 2015, and is updated whenever a policy changes. Superseded versions remain on file for audit purposes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1: EMPLOYMENT CLASSIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Larkspur Films classifies all crew members as either:

- Regular Full-Time: Scheduled for 30 or more hours per week, eligible for all benefits.
- Regular Part-Time: Scheduled for fewer than 30 hours per week, eligible for paid sick leave and retirement plan participation after one year of service.
- Project/Temporary: Hired for a specific production or defined period. Not eligible for health benefits; eligible for paid sick leave as required by Oregon law.
- Daily Hire: Engaged for a single day or a short block of days. Not benefits-eligible.

Classification is determined at time of hire and may be reviewed at the start of each new production. If you believe your classification is incorrect, contact HR within 30 days of receiving your first paycheck.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT ELIGIBILITY & I-9 REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

All employees must complete Form I-9 and present acceptable documentation no later than the third business day after their start date. Start date is recorded as the first day on payroll.

If an employee's work authorization expires during employment, HR must be notified at least two weeks prior to the expiration date. The employee is responsible for providing updated documentation. Failure to do so will result in suspension without pay until valid documentation is presented. If documentation cannot be provided within 30 days of suspension, employment will be terminated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3: COMPENSATION & PAYROLL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pay Periods
- Crew members are paid bi-weekly. Payday falls on the Friday following the end of the pay period.
- Timecards are due to the production office by end of day on the Monday following the close of the pay period. Late timecards will be processed on the next pay cycle.

Overtime
- Oregon law requires overtime pay at 1.5 times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek.
- For productions covered by union collective bargaining agreements, overtime rules from the applicable guild contract supersede state law. Consult your department head or HR for specifics.

Per Diem & Reimbursements
- Per diem is paid for out-of-town shoots at a rate of $50 per day. No receipt is required.
- Mileage reimbursement is $0.55 per mile for use of a personal vehicle on company business. A mileage log must be submitted with the expense report.
- All other reimbursable expenses require an itemized receipt. Receipts must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. Expenses submitted after 30 days may be denied.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4: LEAVE POLICIES
